<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a standard AUR package build process for the `kumiko` terminal emulator. It fetches source code from the official GitHub repository (`https://github.com/iqzer0/kumiko`) and a D language binding package (`gid`) from the official D package registry (`code.dlang.org`), both of which are legitimate upstream sources. The checksums for both sources are provided and match standard practice, indicating no use of 'SKIP' or missing verification.

The build process uses `dub`, the D package manager, to build the application with local sources, which is expected behavior. The `package()` function runs an `install.sh` script from the source tree to install files into the package directory. While running install scripts can carry risk if they contain malicious code, this script is part of the upstream source and no evidence of tampering or obfuscation is present in the PKGBUILD itself. The removal of cache files before installation is a common practice to avoid conflicts, as the system will regenerate them via pacman hooks.

No network operations, dynamic code downloads, or suspicious commands (e.g., `curl|bash`, `eval`, `base64` decoding) are present. All operations are confined to building and packaging the software using standard tools. The package does not modify system files outside of standard installation paths, nor does it exfiltrate data. The use of `dub add-local` is for build dependency management and does not introduce remote code execution risks at build or install time.
</details>
